title: When Zappos Gave Up a Quarter of Its Sales to Stock Its Own Shoes
conflicts: Hsieh's start as co-CEO: 2001 (Swinmurn, Fortune) versus 2000 (company-history entry); Venture Frogs' first money: $500,000 (Swinmurn) versus $1.1 million (company history); the story uses Swinmurn's figures, attributed. The 25% drop-ship share is Hsieh's own figure with no independent check, so it is attributed to him. The Kentucky timeline differs (fulfilment moved there in 2002 per MarketingSherpa; a failed outsourcing arrangement before Zappos ran its own warehouse per the memoir summary); the story does not date the warehouse. 2004 sales: $184 million (Swinmurn) versus 'exceeding $180 million' (company history); the story says 'more than $180 million'.
notes: Founder field credits Swinmurn as the one who started Zappos and Hsieh as early investor and later CEO (worded to avoid a false same-founder match with editions using 'founder'/'chief executive'). Hsieh's memoir and the HBR article were not readable directly; the HBS-platform source is a student analysis used only to support the 2003 dating.
